question: Which approved treatment recovers the most incremental sales in Modern Trade?

economic_constraint.note: ROI must stay above 1.00 across the ENTIRE approved uplift range. Deliberately conservative: the result is a band, not a point, so a scenario that only pays back at the top of its band is not treated as viable.

hierarchy.note: The conservative commercial outcome: what the scenario returns at the weakest uplift its approved rule allows.
Stronger conservative return on the same conservative incremental.
More conservative volume behind the same value.

FINAL TIE-BREAKER ONLY. Trade Spend is NOT an optimisation target: this policy does not hold that lower spend is better, only that between two scenarios equivalent on everything above, the cheaper one is preferred. It appears as supporting evidence regardless.

policy.objective: Prefer a scenario that provides stronger incremental commercial impact while maintaining economically viable promotion performance.
policy.range_policy: Comparisons read the LOW end of the approved uplift range. The high end is supporting context and decides nothing. No midpoint is computed, the band is never collapsed, and it is not a confidence or prediction interval.

provenance.method: Deterministic business rules over results the validated KPI engine produced. No model, no score, no weights.

recommendation.reason: Scenario B is recommended under the current decision policy: among the economically viable scenarios it has the highest conservative incremental sales at the low end of its approved uplift range (₹6.9 Cr). Its ROI stays above break-even across the whole approved range (1.35 at the low end, 1.57 at the high end). Supporting evidence: trade spend ₹5.1 Cr to ₹5.5 Cr across the range.

findings.impact: The approved band returns its investment at both ends.
findings.reason: Low-end uplift clears break-even by 13.1 percentage points. That is above the project's documented narrow-headroom boundary.
findings.source: app/tpo/response.py; scripts/audit_roi_realism.py marks a treatment with less than 2 percentage points of break-even headroom as 'NO MARGIN'. That is the project's own documented boundary, reused here rather than replaced with a new one.
findings.title: Clears break-even across the approved range

findings.impact: The scenario sits inside the approved rules.
findings.reason: PR003 at 15.0% carries an approved uplift range of 40-50%.
findings.title: PR003 is an approved promotion treatment

metrics.label: Incremental Sales
metrics.note: Extensive: weekly values sum to the scope total.

metrics.label: Incremental Units
metrics.note: Extensive: weekly values sum to the scope total.

metrics.label: Trade Spend
metrics.note: Extensive: every row belongs to exactly one week.

metrics.label: Promotion ROI
metrics.note: A RATIO. Never summed and never averaged across weeks. Each week's ROI is computed by the engine from that week's own Incremental Sales and Trade Spend; the scope's ROI is reported separately and is the authority.

metrics.label: Margin Impact
metrics.note: A RATIO of summed revenue and cost. Never summed or averaged; each week is computed from that week's own rows.

metrics.label: Cannibalization Rate
metrics.note: A RATE, and only present when the engine can measure it for the weekly slice. Never summed, never zero-filled.

provenance.method: This is a scenario decomposition across observed business weeks, not a forecast. Each week's figures come from the existing validated KPI engine applied to the same counterfactual rows the aggregate simulation used.
provenance.week_source: WeekRow.week_key, joined from dim_date. fact_sales.Month is never read.

cannibalization.reason: A RATE, and only present when the engine can measure it for the weekly slice. Never summed, never zero-filled.

margin_percent.reason: A RATIO of summed revenue and cost. Never summed or averaged; each week is computed from that week's own rows.

roi_multiple.reason: A RATIO. Never summed and never averaged across weeks. Each week's ROI is computed by the engine from that week's own Incremental Sales and Trade Spend; the scope's ROI is reported separately and is the authority.

reconciliation.note: Additive metrics are summed across weeks and checked against the aggregate simulation. Ratios are never summed or averaged: their weekly values are computed per week by the engine, and the scope figure is reported separately as the authority.

scope.omitted_note: Weeks in scope carrying no promoted row are omitted rather than returned as zeroes: a scenario has no impact to decompose in them.
